verdicts.reason: A uses a sensible two-column banner (product left, 30% OFF/subhead/CTA right) with a clear hierarchy, but the SOLSTICE logo is a near-invisible speck, SUMMER ONLY floats isolated top-right, and the tiny legal sits on top of the brown circle. B stacks everything into a cramped bottom cluster: SUNSET SALE, the CTA and the legal are jammed together and overlap the big ellipse, the legal touches the bottom edge, and the logo is unreadably small.

The two are almost the same: a centred stack with a tiny unreadable logo, an oversized SUMMER ONLY pill as the top focal point, and legal text crammed onto the busy ellipse near the CTA. A keeps a bit more room around the button. In B the legal is pushed against the bottom edge and overlaps the ellipse and circle more.

A has readable headline, subhead and CTA, but its bottom third is cramped: SUNSET SALE, the button and the legal pile onto the busy ellipse, and the logo is a speck. B is simply the original shrunk: the subhead, the CTA label, SUMMER ONLY and the legal are too small to read, and the bottom half is dead space. It is a shrink, not a rearrangement.

A rearranges the design for the format with a clear order (headline, then subhead, SUNSET SALE, product and CTA) and gives the button room, but the logo is nearly invisible, SUMMER ONLY competes at the top, and the tiny legal overlaps the ellipse at the bottom edge. B is the original shrunk uniformly, so the subhead, CTA text and legal are illegible and there is empty space at the bottom.
